turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this screen has frozen again. Please sit, I am just restarting it. What brings you today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, my son Rahul is wheezing after a cold.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Wheezing, is it. Since when? Say that again, I was looking at the login.
[SEG0005] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two weeks, doctor.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Five days.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Two weeks or five days? You are both telling different.
[SEG0008] person_3 (PATIENT): Five.
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am saying two weeks. The sound started with the cold itself.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): I will note roughly five days to two weeks, you two are not agreeing. Any fever with this?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Last night he was feeling hot only, I checked with my hand.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): You say no, amma says hot. Cough is there?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dry cough or with phlegm? Sorry, repeat, the cursor jumped.
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Dry.
[SEG0018] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he was awake half the night, breathing heavy.
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Not half.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then how much, beta? The note did not save.
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): A bit.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay, a bit. Chest pain? Any blood when you cough?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): You are nineteen, no? File is still loading. Asthma from before?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Since class eight only. Last year they did the breathing test, no?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): They said borderline.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Borderline, that is what they told you, not a number on my screen. You stay with parents?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0030] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is in college, computer science. Non-smoker, doctor. We came by auto, traffic was mad.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which inhaler you use when the chest gets tight? Blue or brown?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Brown.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Brown? Say again, I did not hear, someone is knocking also.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Brown.
[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No no, he always mixes them. The blue one he takes for the attack. Brown is the morning-night one.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Blue.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): So finally blue for the attack. How many times in a day are you taking that blue one?
[SEG0038] person_3 (PATIENT): Maybe five, six.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Maybe five, six times a day. That is too much, only. And the brown preventer, daily you are taking?
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Sometimes.
[SEG0041] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He skips, doctor. The brown one is beclomethasone, 200, morning and night.

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me see the prescription scan. Yes, beclomethasone 200 micrograms, one puff twice daily. Salbutamol 100 micrograms, two puffs when needed. You are not taking the brown one properly.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to tablets?
[SEG0045] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0046] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Penicillin, when he was small, red rashes came. We never gave it again.
[SEG0047] person_3 (PATIENT): Don't remember.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. Plan from my side, I will send a chest x-ray today and start amoxicillin 500 milligrams three times a day for five days.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Wait. With this penicillin rash I am not giving amoxicillin. Let me open the sister's peak flow, the screen is slow.
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): It is showing 210... no, that is last year's column, sorry. Sister has read 320 litres, and after the blue puff 410.
[SEG0051] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is 320 very low?
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Predicted for him is about 550, so 320 is low only. There is wheeze both sides, no crackles. I am changing the plan.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): No x-ray today, no antibiotic. I will give a steroid course. Prednisolone 30... actually make it 40 milligrams, by mouth, once every morning after food, for five days.
[SEG0054] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0055] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He has college tests next week. Any problem with the tablet?
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): It can cause a little acidity, so after food only. Do not stop in between.

[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blue inhaler, salbutamol, two puffs when you are wheezy, not five six times. If you need it that often, you must come back. Brown inhaler every morning and night, do not mix the colours.
[SEG0058] person_3 (PATIENT): Brown daily.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): If this does not settle in one week, we might do a chest x-ray. Not now.
[SEG0060] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): When to review?
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let us see in two weeks. If you cannot speak a full sentence or the breathing gets worse, go to casualty, do not wait for me.
[SEG0062] person_3 (PATIENT): Fine.
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): One more time, the system wiped the line. How many times the blue inhaler?
[SEG0064] person_3 (PATIENT): Five, six.
[SEG0065] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And since yesterday he is very tired also.
[SEG0066] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah.

[SEG0067] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tiredness, I have noted. This looks like an asthma flare after the cold, that is my working impression, not a pneumonia. Collect the prednisolone from the pharmacy downstairs.

spec.situation: Teenager or adult wheezy after a cold; confuses blue and brown inhaler; uses the reliever 'maybe five, six times a day'; peak flow numbers read by the nurse. Doctor adds a steroid course.
features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

No fever was denied by the patient when specifically asked.
